types.title: Scholarships
types.intro: Scholarships for undergraduate, master's and PhD study around the world, with who can apply, what they cover and how to apply.
about: A scholarship is money you don't have to pay back. Fully funded scholarships usually cover tuition and a monthly stipend, and the best ones add flights, accommodation and health insurance. Partial scholarships cover only part of tuition, so check what's included before you plan your budget.

Most scholarships are awarded either by governments (such as Chevening, DAAD, MEXT or the Türkiye Burslari) or by universities themselves. Government scholarships often have one central application, while many university awards are given automatically when you apply for admission. Every listing on this page links to the official website, and applying is always free.

types.title: Fellowships
types.intro: Fellowships for students, researchers, young professionals and leaders, with eligibility, benefits and official application links.
about: Fellowships fund people to study, research or work on a project, often for a fixed period. Unlike most scholarships, many fellowships are for graduates and early-career professionals, and some come with a salary-level stipend, training and mentorship.

Fellowships are usually competitive and look closely at your track record and your plans. A strong application shows what you have already done, what you will do during the fellowship and how it will help your community or field afterwards.

types.title: Internships
types.intro: Paid and unpaid internships at international organisations, companies and universities, with who can apply and how.
about: Internships let students and recent graduates gain work experience at international organisations, companies and research centres. Paid internships offer a monthly stipend; unpaid ones may still cover travel or offer remote options.

When you apply, tailor your CV to each role, show the skills the posting asks for and apply early: many internships are filled on a rolling basis. Legitimate internships never charge an application fee.

types.title: Jobs
types.intro: Graduate jobs, traineeships and paid programmes for young people, with requirements and official application links.
about: This page lists graduate jobs, traineeships and paid programmes for young professionals, mostly at international organisations, development banks and large employers. Many are designed for people at the start of their careers and include structured training.
Read each posting carefully for nationality, age and experience requirements, and apply on the employer's own website. Never pay anyone to secure a job offer.

types.title: Competitions
types.intro: Essay, writing, innovation and business competitions with prizes, with entry rules and deadlines.
about: Competitions reward writing, research, innovation and business ideas with cash prizes, trips, mentoring or publication. They are a good way to build your CV, especially when you are still a student.
Follow the rules exactly: word limits, formatting and deadlines are often strict. Original work matters, and many organisers check for plagiarism and AI-generated entries.

types.title: Grants
types.intro: Research grants, project funding and support grants for students and young people.
about: Grants fund a specific piece of work, such as a research project, a community initiative or a small business. They usually require a short proposal explaining what you will do, the budget and the expected results.
Strong grant applications are clear and specific: one problem, a realistic plan, a simple budget and a way to measure success.

types.title: Training and courses
types.intro: Free and funded training programmes, bootcamps and online courses, many with certificates.
about: Free training programmes and online courses help you learn new skills, earn certificates and strengthen scholarship applications. Many top universities publish courses on platforms such as edX and Coursera that you can audit for free.
Certificates sometimes cost a fee, but financial aid is often available. Pick one course, finish it and add it to your CV.

types.title: Conferences
types.intro: Fully funded and partially funded conferences, summits and youth forums.
about: Funded conferences and youth forums cover some or all of your travel, accommodation and registration. They are a chance to present your work, meet people in your field and build a network.
Apply early, keep your abstract or motivation statement focused, and check whether the funding covers visas and flights before you commit.

types.title: Exchange programmes
types.intro: Exchange and summer programmes for students and young leaders, with funding details and how to apply.
about: Exchange and summer programmes let you study, research or take part in leadership training abroad for a few weeks to a year. Many are fully funded for selected participants.
Exchange programmes often have age limits and may require you to be currently enrolled at a university or high school, so read the eligibility rules first.

levels.title: Undergraduate scholarships
levels.label: Undergraduate
levels.intro: Scholarships and opportunities for bachelor's degree study and for current undergraduate students.
about: Undergraduate scholarships help you pay for a bachelor's degree. Some cover the full cost of tuition, accommodation and living expenses, while others reduce tuition by a percentage. Many universities consider you automatically when you apply for admission.

For most undergraduate scholarships you will need your secondary school results, an English test (or proof that you studied in English), a personal statement and recommendation letters. Start early: deadlines for September entry often fall between November and March.

levels.title: Master's scholarships
levels.label: Master's
levels.intro: Fully and partially funded scholarships for master's degrees, with eligibility, documents and official links.
about: Master's scholarships are the most common type of funding for international students. Government programmes such as Chevening, Erasmus Mundus, DAAD and the Eiffel Scholarship fully fund one- or two-year master's degrees, and many universities offer their own awards.
A strong master's application usually includes a good bachelor's degree, a focused motivation letter, a CV, two references and an English test. Some programmes also want work experience.

levels.title: PhD scholarships
levels.label: PhD
levels.intro: Funded PhD positions, doctoral scholarships and fellowships around the world.
about: PhD funding usually comes as a studentship or fellowship that pays your tuition and a monthly stipend for three to four years. In many countries, such as Germany, the Netherlands and the Nordic countries, PhD positions are paid jobs with a salary.
Most PhD applications depend on finding a supervisor and writing a clear research proposal. Contact potential supervisors early and tailor your proposal to their research.

levels.title: High school scholarships
levels.label: High school
levels.intro: Scholarships, competitions and programmes for secondary school students.
about: High school opportunities include scholarships, exchange years, summer schools and competitions for secondary school students. Some are fully funded and give students a first experience of studying abroad.
Many programmes have strict age limits and need a parent's or guardian's consent, so check the rules carefully before applying.

audiences.title: Scholarships for Nigerians
audiences.label: Nigerians
audiences.intro: Opportunities Nigerians can apply for: ones only for Nigerians, plus ones open to Africans and to developing countries.
about: This page collects opportunities that Nigerians can apply for: ones only for Nigerians, plus ones open to Africans and to developing countries. Opportunities open to every nationality are listed separately under scholarships for international students.
Always check the official eligibility list, because some international programmes exclude certain countries.

audiences.title: Scholarships for Africans
audiences.label: Africans
audiences.intro: Scholarships, internships and programmes open to African students and young professionals.
about: These scholarships, internships and programmes are open to students and young professionals from African countries, including many Mastercard Foundation and DAAD programmes.
Some programmes cover only sub-Saharan Africa, and others only specific countries, so check that your country is listed.

audiences.title: Scholarships for developing countries
audiences.label: Developing countries
audiences.intro: Opportunities for citizens of developing, low-income and middle-income countries.
about: These opportunities are for citizens of developing, low-income and middle-income countries, often based on the OECD's list of countries eligible for development aid.
Check the official country list for each programme, because the eligible countries can change from year to year.

audiences.title: Scholarships for women
audiences.label: Women
audiences.intro: Scholarships, fellowships and programmes just for women and girls.
about: These scholarships, fellowships and programmes are only for women and girls, many in science, technology, engineering and leadership.
Some are also limited to certain countries or fields, so read each listing's eligibility section.

audiences.title: Scholarships for international students
audiences.label: All nationalities
audiences.intro: Opportunities open to students of any nationality.
about: These opportunities are open to students of any nationality. Some still have limits based on where you live, your age or your field of study.
Read the eligibility section of each listing carefully before you apply.
